solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Criminal dupes everyone initially, including old policemen, in faked death

indicators.note: including says the old policemen are held within the other letters
criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters of dupes are rearranged
initially points to the opening letter of the word everyone

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the UK's plain-clothes detectives

explanation.surface: A con artist fools everybody, police included, by staging their own demise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a description of the swindler, but it is the anagram signal; CID is Britain's plain-clothes detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Pseudocide is the act of faking one's own death, typically to escape debts or the law.

clue.text: Zoo abandoned boring marketing relating to ears of early lifeforms

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the rearranged letters go inside the other pieces

parts.note: PR, public relations, is a kind of marketing
otic is the adjective for things relating to the ear

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained behaviour, so the letters of zoo are rearranged

explanation.surface: An abandoned zoo seems tedious to a marketing department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' reads as dull, but it means drilling in: the scrambled zoo goes inside the marketing-plus-ears pieces, after their fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Protozoic was the geological era named for the earliest forms of animal life, so the adjective describes primitive organisms.

clue.text: Throw out unopened item that's unsuitable for sale

indicators.note: unopened means the word loses its first letter, its opening

parts.note: a reject is a faulty item that cannot be sold

explanation.surface: Discard a sealed product that has proved unsellable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' removes the R that begins REJECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject is to expel or throw someone or something out forcibly.

clue.text: Twin reckons they start at ten

parts.note: twin means a double, an exact counterpart
to figure is to reckon or calculate, so figures means reckons

explanation.surface: One of a pair of twins makes a guess about something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: numbers in double figures run from 10 upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Double figures are the two-digit numbers, the lowest of which is ten.

clue.text: Crack team reduced criminal activity

indicators.note: reduced says the word for team is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a crew is a team, as of rowers or workers
vice is criminal activity such as prostitution or gambling, as policed by a vice squad

explanation.surface: An elite squad has cut down on lawbreaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like an adjective for the team, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevice is a narrow opening or fissure, as in rock.

clue.text: Girl from the south claims gold ahead of American model

indicators.note: ahead of puts the gold-holding piece before the American
claims means takes in, so one piece holds another
in a down clue, from the south means read from the bottom up, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a maid is a girl or young woman
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A southern girl stakes a claim to gold before an American model does.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'from the south' means read upwards; OR as gold comes from heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional scale model of a scene, as in a museum display.

clue.text: Wife interrupts to undermine exchange

indicators.note: interrupts means breaks into, so this letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: to sap is to undermine or weaken gradually

explanation.surface: A wife cuts in to sabotage a conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to trade one thing for another, an exchange.

clue.text: Dedication to the task of shifting white rock

indicators.note: shifting means moving about, so the letters of white rock are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone diligently moves pale stone about.
explanation.definitionFit: A work ethic is a belief in the value of hard work, a commitment to getting the job done.

clue.text: Publicity campaign

definitions.meaning: newspaper coverage, so publicity in the media

explanation.surface: A publicity campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: Press covers both media attention and the act of urging hard for a cause.

clue.text: Exposed novel and deceptive plan for excessive exploitation

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters of novel are removed

parts.note: a ruse is a deceptive plan or trick

explanation.surface: A racy novel and a cunning scheme lead to someone being used too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exposed' strips the N and L from NOVEL, leaving OVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Overuse is use beyond what is reasonable, so wearing something out by exploiting it too much.

clue.text: Monitor of mad cow disease upset over cases

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so the rearranged letters wrap round the disease
upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters of over are rearranged

parts.note: BSE, bovine spongiform encephalopathy, is mad cow disease

explanation.surface: Someone watches an outbreak of mad cow disease, troubled by the number of cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' looks like instances of the disease, but it means encloses: the shuffled ORVE wraps round the disease after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to watch carefully, the job of anyone keeping tabs on something.

clue.text: Wrong part of flight, it seems, to misbehave

parts.note: a flight of stairs is made of steps
out of line means wrong or improper

explanation.surface: Someone missteps on a staircase and seems to be acting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' means a staircase here, not air travel.
explanation.definitionFit: To step out of line is to behave inappropriately or break the rules.

clue.text: Base representation of short story on company heading west

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so the shortened story comes second
in an across clue heading west means read right to left, so the word is reversed
short means the word for story loses its last letter

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A short story about a firm moving west, as a basic version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' is a number base: octal writes numbers in base eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Octal is the base-eight numeral system, a way of representing numbers in that base.

clue.text: Absurdity of acting is seen to entertain grandma

indicators.note: to entertain is to take in as a guest, so one piece holds another
acting means performing a role, so the letters of is seen play a different part

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother

explanation.surface: The ridiculousness of a performance is shown up when Granny is amused by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acting' turns IS SEEN into IENESS, which takes in NAN after its I.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or senseless, so inaneness is foolishness or ridiculousness.

clue.text: Description of eleven in succession

definitions.meaning: the numeral 11 is one figure 1 written after another

explanation.surface: A description of eleven in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Things happening one after another happen consecutively, each following the last.

clue.text: Surveying tool for cutting, climbing and excavating

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: an axe is a tool for cutting wood
mining is digging or excavating

explanation.surface: A tool used for cutting, rock climbing and digging.
explanation.definitionFit: Examining is inspecting closely, as in surveying a site or a document.

clue.text: Strange one resolved without using advanced radiation units

indicators.note: resolved means worked out afresh, so the letters are rearranged
without using says one letter is left out of the rearranged pool

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: An odd person sorts out a problem without help from anyone more experienced.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange STRANGE ONE minus the A that 'without using advanced' removes.
explanation.definitionFit: The roentgen is an old unit of exposure to X-rays and gamma rays, named after their discoverer.

clue.text: Quickly ran parking report — something influenced by Teslas

parts.note: to charge is to rush forward, so charged means ran quickly
an article is a report in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A hurried news story about parking an electric Tesla car.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla suggests the car maker, but here it is the unit of magnetic flux density.
explanation.definitionFit: A charged particle such as an electron is deflected by magnetic fields, measured in teslas.

clue.text: Wooden vessel is beyond late

indicators.note: is beyond means comes after, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late king
a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: A wooden bowl is past its use-by date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wooden' looks like a material for the vessel, but it means expressionless.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan face shows no emotion, the same stiff look as a wooden performance.

clue.text: Old half of NY borough opposed to caps

indicators.note: in a down clue caps means sits on top of, so this piece goes before the other

parts.note: anti means opposed to

indicators.note: half of means only the first half of the word's letters is used

parts.note: Queens is one of the five boroughs of New York City

explanation.surface: Elderly residents of a New York borough are against hats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes QUE from QUEENS.
explanation.definitionFit: An antique is an old object, and as an adjective it means old-fashioned or of a past era.

clue.text: Emperor leans over, grabbing duck to cook on rotisserie

indicators.note: grabbing means holding on to, so the reversed letters close round the duck
over means turned over, so the words for emperor and leans are read backwards

parts.note: a tsar was an emperor of Russia
to tip is to tilt or lean
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: An emperor bends down to seize a duck for roasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses both words together, giving SPITRAST; 'duck' is a cricket score of nought, so O.
explanation.definitionFit: To spit-roast is to cook meat on a rotating spit, which is what a rotisserie does.

clue.text: Guy accepts first-class fare from Indonesia

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a guy is a rope used to steady something, also called a stay
A is the top grade, so first-class

explanation.surface: A man agrees to first-class food from Indonesia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man, but it is a supporting rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Satay is an Indonesian dish of skewered grilled meat with peanut sauce.

clue.text: Duke welcomes king before everybody else

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the king goes inside the other word

parts.note: in rhyming slang dukes are fists, from Duke of Yorks for forks, slang for hands
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A duke greets the king ahead of all the other guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duke' looks like a nobleman, but it is a fist, from Cockney rhyming slang.
explanation.definitionFit: First means ahead of all others in order or time.

clue.text: Nosey beast is surely not following current personnel around

indicators.note: following means this piece comes after the other
around means turned round, so the words for current and personnel are read backwards

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
HR, human resources, is the personnel department
no is a flat refusal, surely not

explanation.surface: A nosy creature is not after the staff who are about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nosey' points to the beast's famous horned snout; I is the physics symbol for current.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros is known for its large horned nose, hence a nosey beast.

clue.text: Makes mistake outing son at university

parts.note: a trip is an outing or excursion
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Someone errs by disclosing that their son is a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outing' suggests revealing a secret, but it is a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip up is to make an error or blunder.

clue.text: Briefly stop using square medication

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to quit is to stop using something
nine is a square number, three times three

explanation.surface: Someone is told to give up a remedy quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Quinine is a drug made from cinchona bark, used to treat malaria.

clue.text: Way of meditating unknown back in the past

parts.note: y is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: back means the word for in the past is read in reverse

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: An unknown form of meditation from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga is a Hindu discipline of breathing, posture and meditation.

clue.text: Meagre pungent herb not lush when all peeled

indicators.note: peeled means skinned, so each of the four words loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A sharp herb that is not lush is a poor thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when all peeled' leaves UNGEN, ER, O and US.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungenerous means mean or stingy, offering little, so meagre.
